arms.hypothesis: if GDN run-to-run nondeterminism were an ordering race, a completion barrier would fix it far cheaper than serializing the recurrence
arms.verdict: The completion barrier does not repair the failure. It costs about 1 tok/s (97.211 vs 98.222), while the divergent prompts and token positions are byte-identical to the no-barrier run -- same 8 reported prompt/token pairs. This rules out a missing end-of-op completion dependency as the explanation; it does not by itself identify GDN reduction order or separate GDN from the simultaneously disabled global batch-invariant policies.
no gain (91.371 vs 91.926). The MTP draft head was not padding one-row forwards to four; hypothesis wrong.

optimization_ladder_20260818.conclusion: Validated best under a fresh-compile gate remains 91.926 tok/s at 25/25 self-determinism. The 97-98 tok/s arms do not reproduce across FRESH compile caches. The other machine correctly noted that the fast arm disabled serial-exact GDN and global batch invariance together, so the 6.3 tok/s and the divergence were not causally separated between those two flags -- that attribution is still open. However the divergence itself is now explained: rerunning the fast arm against the FIRST arm's compile cache reproduced it exactly, 25/25 over 12413 tokens. The nondeterminism is in compilation, not runtime. See root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.

root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.finding: The run-to-run nondeterminism that has gated this and the Qwen3.6 lane is in torch.compile/Inductor COMPILATION, not at runtime. Given a fixed compiled artifact the runtime is perfectly deterministic.
root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.corroboration: The divergent prompts and token positions were byte-identical between the completion-barrier and no-barrier experiments. Random runtime noise would not repeat positions across configs; two different-but-internally-deterministic compilations would, and do.
root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.why_serial_exact_looked_necessary: serial-exact GDN forces that op to an EAGER graph break, so it is never compiled and never autotuned. It was not buying arithmetic determinism -- it was avoiding the compiler.
root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.methodological_consequence: The compiled cache is part of the run identity, exactly like the .so binaries the harness already pins by hash. A deployed service compiles once and serves that artifact; reproducibility across restarts with a pinned cache is the operationally meaningful property. This tightens the identity requirement rather than relaxing the gate.

latent_bug_replayssm_ring_length.severity: latent - not triggered here because the spec arm sets VLLM_XPU_GDN_REPLAYSSM_SPEC=0
latent_bug_replayssm_ring_length.detail: run-tp2-targetgraph-drafteager-candidate.sh:45 derives VLLM_XPU_GDN_REPLAYSSM_SPEC_CACHE_LEN as 2*(num_speculative_tokens+1). Its own comment at :44 says callers may request a larger POWER-OF-TWO ring. For MTP3 that yields 8, a power of two. For MTP4 it yields 10 and for MTP5 12, neither a power of two.
latent_bug_replayssm_ring_length.impact: anyone enabling ReplaySSM at depth != 3 gets a non-power-of-two ring, contradicting the documented contract
latent_bug_replayssm_ring_length.suggested_fix: round the derived length up to the next power of two

harness_defect_quality_baseline_substitu.severity: high - silently graded a model against a DIFFERENT model's baseline
harness_defect_quality_baseline_substitu.detail: run-tp2-targetgraph-drafteager-candidate.sh:67 and run-tp1-current-candidate.sh:56 used ${QUALITY_BASELINE_JSON:-<qwen36 baseline>}. The :- form substitutes on EMPTY as well as unset, so omitting the baseline argument silently graded the run against the Qwen3.6 model's quality baseline instead of running without one.
harness_defect_quality_baseline_substitu.impact: every Qwen3.8 quality result recorded before this fix, including the pass_all/baseline_match_all values reported for the 91.926, 98.222 and MTP4 arms, was compared against the Qwen3.6 baseline. Those runs did pass, which is a meaningful cross-model observation, but it is NOT a model-specific quality gate.
harness_defect_quality_baseline_substitu.fix: changed :- to - so an explicitly empty value means no baseline

root_cause_persistent_gdn_scratch.bug: uninitialized read in the persistent GDN spec-decode scratch at 5 verifier rows (MTP4)
evidence: with scratch ON, MTP4 was 24/25 across all three pairs, always failing on holdout--long-rollover-repository-audit
the divergence position moved between run pairs (88, 30, 30), which a deterministic arithmetic difference cannot do
the same prompt run in a 2-prompt suite was IDENTICAL across runs, so the fault is history dependent
setting VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_PERSISTENT_SCRATCH=0 gives 25/25 across all three pairs AND is faster
root_cause_persistent_gdn_scratch.interpretation: the scratch is cached across calls and a region is read before being written at 5 rows, so results depend on whatever the allocator left there. MTP3 at 4 rows writes the whole region, which is why it was clean.
root_cause_persistent_gdn_scratch.WARNING_FOR_SERIAL_EXACT_WORK: gdn_attn_interface.cpp requires VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_PERSISTENT_SCRATCH=1 whenever serial-exact is enabled. Any MTP4-with-serial-exact build will therefore hit this same uninitialized scratch. The scratch must be zero-initialised, or sized/written correctly for k+1 rows, before that path can be trusted.
